parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Kenpoly-sec-school-field, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1874 | 2.78 | 2.78
2 | 2428 | 9.13 | 11.9
3 | 1071 | 15.2 | 27.1
4 | 3706 | 32.2 | 59.3
5 | 178 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Kenpoly-sec-school-field, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report: Kenpoly-sec-school-field, Bori Metropolis**

The vertical electrical sounding (VES) survey reveals a five-layer geoelectric section:
- **Layer 1:** 1874 $\Omega\cdot$m, thickness 2.78 m (topsoil).
- **Layer 2:** 2428 $\Omega\cdot$m, thickness 9.13 m (depth to base 11.9 m).
- **Layer 3:** 1071 $\Omega\cdot$m, thickness 15.2 m (depth to base 27.1 m).
- **Layer 4:** 3706 $\Omega\cdot$m, thickness 32.2 m (depth to base 59.3 m).
- **Layer 5:** 178 $\Omega\cdot$m (underlying formation).

Evaluation of consecutive three-layer resistivity relationships:
- Layers 1–3 ($r_1 < r_2 > r_3$): K-type
- Layers 2–4 ($r_2 > r_3 < r_4$): H-type
- Layers 3–5 ($r_3 < r_4 > r_5$): K-type

The resulting sequence yields a KHK-type curve, which is fully consistent with the classification on file.

{"curve_type_stated": "KHK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
